summary: Midday surge of 5xxs caused by API gateway throttle cascade and runtime hot-loop overload
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10 12:08 UTC we observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the hosted API for a set of dedicated customers. Error rate rose from <0.2% to ~8% across a 6-minute window and remained elevated for ~30 minutes before partial mitigation. Impact: Customer-facing requests for BrightWrite (dedicated tenant) experienced timeouts and 502/503 responses; streaming sessions were abruptly reset, and embeds/bulk operations observed retries. Environment: production us-east, dedicated pool for BrightWrite. Initial hypothesis: API gateway token bucket exhaustion combined with upstream runtime entering a CPU-bound hot-loop while processing prefetch invalidations, leading to backpressure and retry amplification.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a mixed workload from a single tenant with concurrent small-chat streams (keepalive) + large embedding batch uploads at 400 req/s
2) Ensure model pinning to redwood/gptx-13b-instruct and prefetch enabled
3) Observe gateway metrics and runtime process CPU/RSS over a sustained burst (2-10 minutes)
Expected: transient queueing but <1% 5xx. Observed: rapid growth to ~8% 5xx and sustained elevated errors until mitigation steps applied.
logs: 2026-03-10T12:08:21Z apigw: token-bucket refill lag detected tenant=brightwrite delta=-220ms failures=124
2026-03-10T12:09:03Z runtime[worker-7]: WARN hotloop detected: prefetch-invalidations processing count=87 cpu=94% pid=23211
2026-03-10T12:12:31Z runtime[worker-3]: ERROR failed to service request: OOM avoidance triggered, kill-kv-cache-temp, stacktrace...
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between large embedding bulk uploads (300MB payloads) and token-bucket refill lag on apigw for the dedicated tenant.

Prefetch-cache sweep routine triggered simultaneous invalidations for the tenant's pinned model; several runtime workers entered a tight loop handling invalidation tombstones (heap churn + CPU spike).
API gateway responded to upstream slowness by tightening token bucket allocation which created a feedback loop: more clients retried, causing broader enqueue growth and runtime saturation.

No recent deploys to serving-runtime in the 24h preceding the incident; a config sweep to prefetch thresholds rolled out earlier at 08:00 UTC but looked low risk (rollout ID infra-roll/2026-03-10-08).
Heap/driver OOMs observed on two workers; NVML reports no GPU OOMs — issue appears CPU/queueing dominated rather than GPU memory.
Can reproduce a smaller-scale failure in staging by replaying tenant traffic mix with accelerated timing; staging experiment shows gateway token-bucket hits at ~120 req/s in test config.
comments: Aisha Kapoor (Support): Received alert at 12:08 UTC; triaged and alerted SRE. Customer BrightWrite reports high 502s on their production integration.

Maya Chen (SRE): Confirmed token-bucket refill lag and runtime CPU hotloop; started mitigations: reduced prefetch sweep window for the tenant, opened ephemeral extra workers, and escalated to runtime on-call.
Elliot Park (Runtime eng): Hotloop traced to prefetch tombstone iteration path; added short-circuit to break long invalidation sequences. Preparing a hotfix branch. Reference PR in investigation.
Maya Chen (SRE): Applied temporary apigw route-rate cap for BrightWrite to limit retry amplification at 12:20 UTC — error rate dropped to ~1.7% within 6 minutes.
Customer BrightWrite (via CS): Acknowledged partial recovery at 12:30 UTC; requested postmortem and confirmation that embedding uploads will be throttled to avoid recurrence.
actions_taken: 12:12 UTC - Reduced prefetch invalidation concurrency for dedicated pool to 2 workers (temporary).
12:20 UTC - Applied per-tenant apigw soft-rate cap and bumped keepalive limits to reduce churn.
12:26 UTC - Added two ephemeral runtime workers to absorb backlog and processed queued invalidations with backoff.
12:40 UTC - Reverted emergency caps after steady state confirmed and coordinated with customer for controlled upload retry window.
next_steps: 1) Runtime team to land PR that short-circuits long prefetch invalidation loops (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987).
2) API gateway to include better per-tenant burst detection and adaptive refill logic (infra ticket INT-330-priority).
3) Add customer-facing guidance to dedicated onboarding: recommended max concurrent embedding payloads and use of chunked uploads.
4) Run a post-incident capacity test with BrightWrite's traffic profile in staging and verify apigw token-bucket behavior under mixed load.
5) Update runbook: include explicit steps for 'prefetch invalidation hotloop' and apigw soft-cap play.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied; full code fix in review. Customer agreed to coordinated upload throttling pending runtime fix.
resolution_notes: Mitigation sequence reduced error rate to acceptable SLA levels. Runtime fix (short-circuit) is in PR and targeted for canary deploy 2026-03-13. Follow-up: scheduled capacity test with BrightWrite on 2026-03-15. No billing adjustments requested by the customer at this time.
